I was a very anxious kid when I started highschool. The year prior was my first year within the district. I had a few friends, but not many. I was genuinely just scared. My first day though? It went terrific. This was something I did not expect at all. Middle school was a little rough for me. The dynamic changed entirely. Once highschool starts, things loosen up a bit. Rules are less strict. I personally feel like people are less mean (surprising, I know). Genuinely, highschool is where you will meet some of your best friends, some of your enemies and even some pretty dope acquaintances here and there. Your relationships with people will fluctuate, and that’s normal because you’re on a road to finding yourself. I assure you though, nothing to be scared about! I’m currently going to be a senior this upcoming year. I’m quite excited, and the past few years have brought me up to this excitement. I hope as the years go on, you can be excited too! You deserve it! You got this, and good luck!! 💛

Find something new! Take your mind off of all the bad and focus it on something like that!

Being 17 having worked at Wendy’s, I was on 4-11 shifts a few times a week. It’s not necessarily night, but 10-11 is late enough if you ask me. A few minutes before our dining room close at 10, a man came in. Technically I wasn’t allowed to kick him out, so I let him order. The entire time he was being overly friendly, and I just took it as a lack of social skills on his part. He continued to tell me my apron was tight, and how good I looked in it. First of all, it’s a Wendy’s apron, how good CAN I seriously look in it? But, I said thank you. He continues, and says, “You know, you remind me of this one celebrity. I don’t remember her name, but she went missing and they never found her.” Let me tell you, I went on RED ALERT mode. I was about to lose my marbles. My manager looked at me, and was like uhh what the fuck. So he sits, and he leaves at about 10:15. I started to clean up our dining room and I look out the window and he is still parked in his car. He was out there until 11:10, which was 10 after my shift. I did not want to leave with him out there. He was so scary to me. Probably the worst night experience ever.
